OncoCohortSelect

OncoCohortSelect selects one of several single-arm oncology cohorts with multiple efficacy and safety endpoints for further development, and evaluates the selection rules by simulation.

Methods

  • Posterior benefit-risk score (Chakraborty et al., 2026). Each component is the posterior probability that an endpoint is favorable: a response or adverse event rate (beta-binomial model), a survival probability at a given time or a hazard ratio (exponential model with a gamma prior of the hazard). The components are computed against target values for each cohort, or relative to a reference cohort, and combined by a weighted geometric mean; admissibility cutoffs can be set for each component.
  • Generalized pairwise comparisons (Buyse, 2010) of prioritized binary and time-to-event endpoints with the scoring rule of Gehan or of Péron et al. (2018): the net treatment benefit, the win ratio and the win odds, with standard errors from the U-statistic theory. Any number of endpoints, any priority order and thresholds for time-to-event endpoints can be used.
  • Simulation. Correlated progression-free survival, overall survival and objective response are generated for each cohort with the CorOncoEndpoints package, an adverse event independent of them is added, and the data are cut at a calendar time of analysis. Two or more cohorts are compared with a reference cohort, and the decision rules are compared at a common probability of selecting a cohort that is not better than the reference.
  • Data of a completed trial can use columns coded as in ADaM data sets, such as censoring indicators (CNSR) and the best overall response.

Installation

OncoCohortSelect and the package it uses to simulate correlated endpoints, CorOncoEndpoints, are installed from GitHub; neither is on CRAN.

install.packages("remotes")
# CorOncoEndpoints, at the version used by OncoCohortSelect
remotes::install_github("gosukehommaEX/CorOncoEndpoints@35f731d6052ff31625c140af0018b2558142dfc3")
remotes::install_github("gosukehommaEX/OncoCohortSelect")

The second call alone also installs CorOncoEndpoints at this version, which is fixed in the Remotes field of DESCRIPTION; the first call makes the dependency explicit. CorOncoEndpoints contains C++ code and is built from source, so Rtools is needed on Windows.

Example 

library(OncoCohortSelect)

arms <- list(
  Cohort1 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 8, orr = 0.45, resp.cor = 0.4,
                                      death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 18),
  Cohort2 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 6, orr = 0.30, resp.cor = 0.4,
                                      death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 15))
d <- SimCohorts(nsim = 1, n = c(50, 50), arms = arms, ae.rate = c(0.35, 0.20),
                cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = 1)

eps <- list(Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),
            Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),
            Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
            Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))

# benefit-risk score against target values
crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                   target = c(0.30, 0.50, 0.60, 0.30), time = c(NA, 6, 12, NA))
BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit)

# benefit-risk score of Cohort1 relative to Cohort2
crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                       measure = c("rate", "hr", "hr", "rate"),
                       target = c(0.10, 0.80, 0.90, 0.10))
BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit_ref, reference = "Cohort2")

# net treatment benefit, win ratio and win odds (priority OS, PFS, ORR, AE)
w <- WinStat(d, eps, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2")
w
plot(w)

# censored pairs scored with the Kaplan-Meier estimates (Peron)
WinStat(d, eps, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2", scoring = "peron")$ci

Columns coded as in ADaM data sets are named in Endpoint():

Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "OSAVAL", censor = "OSCNSR")
Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "BOR", positive = c("CR", "PR"))
Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "AEFL", positive = "Y", higher.better = FALSE)

Functions

Function Purpose
Endpoint() Define a binary or time-to-event endpoint
PosteriorProb() Posterior probability that a rate, survival probability or hazard ratio is favorable
BenefitRisk() Component probabilities, admissibility and composite benefit-risk score of cohorts
WinStat() Net treatment benefit, win ratio and win odds of prioritized endpoints
SimCohorts() Simulate cohorts with correlated PFS, OS and response and an adverse event
SimSelection() Benefit-risk scores and win statistics of simulated trials, for two or more cohorts against a reference cohort
SelectionOC() Probability that a decision rule selects each cohort
CalibrateThreshold() Threshold of a decision rule for a given probability of selecting a cohort other than the reference

The results of BenefitRisk(), WinStat(), SimSelection() and SelectionOC() have print() and plot() methods.

Verification

  • tests/testthat: expected values computed independently in Python (inst/validation/python), the example of Section S.4 of the supplementary material of Chakraborty et al. (2026), hand calculations, and comparisons with the BuyseTest package (Gehan and Péron scoring rules).
  • inst/reproduce/reproduce_published.R: reproduction of published numbers.
  • inst/validation/validate_posterior.R: Monte Carlo check of the posterior probabilities.
  • inst/validation/validate_winstat.R: comparison of the win statistics with BuyseTest on simulated trials, with the Gehan and Péron scoring rules.
  • inst/validation/validate_simcohorts.R: Monte Carlo check of the simulated cohorts.

A two-stage dose optimization framework for oncology drug development with multiple efficacy and safety endpoints via an integrated benefit-risk assessment. Péron, J., Buyse, M., Ozenne, B., Roche, L. and Roy, P. (2018). An extension of generalized pairwise comparisons for prioritized outcomes in the presence of censoring. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 27, 1230-1239. https://doi.org/10.1177/0962280216658320
